doc.title: Rusty Dedrick interviewed by Monk Rowe, Ellenville, New York, June 23, 1998

title: Writing for Thornhill and Gil Evans
summary: Thornhill gave him a free hand and paid more than Norvo; he copied parts himself.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: Did you continue writing for all the bands you—

Oh yeah. Then Claude of course was a great, great writer himself. And Gil Evans joined the band. But still Claude gave me a free hand, and he paid more money too. He was more appreciative of the effort that goes into making arrangements than Red.
You copied all the parts yourself?
And not at a computer, either.
